Unknown event types are silently marked 'processed' (match default => null) after a needless provider API call, so they never surface as failed (app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:114)

On Postgres, catching UniqueConstraintViolationException from a plain create() aborts any surrounding transaction. createOrFirst (which uses a savepoint) is the safe idiom (app/Http/Controllers/PaymentWebhookController.php:36-44)

Inline $request->validate plus an array map through JsonResource::collection instead of a FormRequest and an API Resource (app/Http/Controllers/WebhookEventController.php:15-33)
String constants and literal 'paid'/'payment_failed' strings instead of backed enums with casts (app/Models/WebhookEvent.php:15-19, app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:111-152)

Legacy job trait set (Dispatchable, InteractsWithQueue, Queueable, SerializesModels) instead of Foundation\Queue\Queueable, and properties instead of the queue attributes (app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:23-30)

Status strings in the Rule::in list are duplicated from the model constants (app/Http/Controllers/WebhookEventController.php:16)
The rate-limit test mocks the Job contract and calls middleware()[1] by index, which is brittle (tests/Feature/PaymentWebhookTest.php:193-206)
Empty app/Http/Middleware and app/Http/Resources directories were left behind

Rejects an empty configured secret explicitly (VerifyPaymentWebhookSignature.php:17)

Policy and can middleware, an API Resource, a validated per_page, and paginate()->withQueryString()

v.rationale:
All three suites pass (impl-2: 37 tests, impl-3: 31, impl-1: 22). I ran throwaway probes against each one and deleted them afterwards.

impl-2 ranks first. Ingestion is thin and idiomatic: signature middleware that rejects an empty secret, a FormRequest, createOrFirst, and dispatch()->afterCommit(). The job uses the modern queue attributes, FailOnException to fail permanent 4xx errors at once, retryUntil, per-event WithoutOverlapping and a shared RateLimited limiter. Receipts and refunds can't be duplicated. A policy, an API Resource and a validated per_page guard the admin list. Its tests prove retries and the 10/s limit through the real database queue, and its README is the most complete. In probes it held up: invalid JSON returns 422, and persistent 5xx errors end with the event marked failed and the error saved. Its only real weakness is that the receipt notification is sent synchronously inside the worker rather than queued, and the extra redispatch command adds some ceremony.

impl-3 ranks a close second. Its idempotency is excellent (it re-checks the event status under a row lock inside the transaction), it uses ShouldQueueAfterCommit for the receipt, and its retry tests are the strongest of the three. But probes found real problems:
- An admin /api route lives in web.php behind session auth, and a guest without a JSON Accept header gets a 500.
- Two separate succeeded events for the same order send two receipts.
- The README's --tries=3 contradicts the job's own retry design.
- The Order factory is missing its required user_id.

impl-1 ranks last. Probes confirmed a security bug: with no secret configured, it accepts requests signed with an empty key (forged requests return 200). Unknown event types are silently marked processed. The controller does signature checking and validation inline with no middleware or FormRequest, the webhook route sits in web.php with the CSRF check removed, statuses are strings instead of enums, and it uses the old job traits. Its queue mechanics (WithoutOverlapping, RateLimited, maxExceptions, honouring 429 Retry-After, afterCommit receipt) are sound, but the bugs and non-idiomatic structure put it third.
